newsitem.title: KENYA: 19 countries urge dialogue over reforms in Kenya.
newsitem.headline: 19 countries urge dialogue over reforms in Kenya.

text.p: Members of the European Union and six other countries condemned violence and urged Kenya's government to open dialogue with groups demanding constitutional reforms.

Thirteen European Union member states, the European Commission, Canada, Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Japan, Norway and Switzerland urged the government and those advocating reform to refrain from violence.
"It is the responsibility of the government of Kenya to protect not only the safety of Kenyan citizens but also their human and civil rights," the embassies said in a statement.

"A meaningful dialogue and a more liberal implementation of the existing laws are in the opinion of the undersigned foreign missions the best way to protect the safety as well as the human and civic rights of Kenyans," they said.
"The undersigned foreign missions therefore urge the government to initiate a dialogue with those advocating reform."

Nine people were killed on Monday during the worst day of violent clashes in Kenya for seven years when riot police broke up rallies called by groups demanding constitutional reforms before presidential and parliamentary elections this year.
Students clashed with riot police on Tuesday night and on Wednesday until authorities closed the University of Nairobi.

The embassies condemned violent disturbances in several Kenyan cities this week and said they were shocked by deaths, the large number of injured, the use of live ammunition by police and the storming of All Saints Cathedral.

They said they were very concerned about the escalation of political violence in Kenya and renewed a call on the government and those advocating reforms to refrain from violence and resort to peaceful means.

"A dialogue should be seen by all parties as the only means to reach a solution," they said. President Daniel arap Moi says constitutional reforms cannot be considered until after the general election.
